lines: Take {gift_item}. Good gear should travel, not gather dust.
Here, {gift_item}. It has more use with you than sitting by my cauldron.
Take {gift_item}. It is not much, but it is given with care.
Most days, I am at the cauldron, trying to keep stitching and straps from becoming everyone else's problem.
People think leather is simple until something goes wrong and suddenly it is very important.
A village runs on small work. Nobody praises it until it stops happening.
I trust a good needle more than a loud promise. The needle has less to prove.
If you want my honest answer, slow down first. Rushed questions usually hide worse ones.
The village looks calm from a distance. Up close, it is mostly chores arguing with weather.
I notice the little things. That is either a skill or what the cauldron has done to me.
